decision: read-only HTTPS mission telemetry with explicit owner-session bootstrap
context: The iPhone app needs visibility into distributed mission state without becoming a new authority boundary before Qubes worker semantics are proven. The server /api/missions endpoint is owner-authenticated, so the phone must establish the existing cookie session rather than inventing a second authentication scheme.

approaches.name: existing owner cookie session + read-only HTTPS snapshot
approaches.correctness: strongest separation: phone authenticates through /api/auth, then only performs GET /api/missions; worker mutation remains exclusively server-side
approaches.robustness: fail-closed on non-HTTPS, malformed response, non-2xx, expired session, missing revision, or unavailable telemetry
approaches.latency: one bounded auth status GET and one bounded mission GET per refresh; login only when session is absent or expired
approaches.resourceUse: low; shared URLSession cookie handling and no persistent socket/background daemon
approaches.regressionRisk: low; reuses established server authentication and adds no new authorization semantics
approaches.qa: Node contract tests verify HTTPS-only access, GET-only mission telemetry, 401 handling, no password persistence, and no worker mutation controls; native Swift build remains a separate environment gate

approaches.name: new bearer or pairing token dedicated to mission telemetry
approaches.correctness: can work but duplicates authentication and revocation semantics
approaches.robustness: would require new token issuance, storage, rotation, scope, expiration, and revocation logic
approaches.latency: slightly fewer auth requests after token provisioning
approaches.regressionRisk: medium-high because it creates another credential path

approaches.name: bidirectional command API or websocket from iPhone
approaches.correctness: weaker at this stage because it creates a second mutation/ordering boundary
approaches.robustness: requires durable nonce/replay protection, command fencing, reconnect ordering, and reconciliation
approaches.qa: deferred until worker boundary is REAL-WORKER READY

winnerReason: Reusing the existing HttpOnly Secure SameSite owner session is the strongest approach because it closes the actual integration gap without weakening server controls or creating a new credential system. The dashboard remains read-only, requires HTTPS, does not persist the typed owner password, and relies on the server's existing 12-hour session cookie.
failuresAndLessons: The first MissionControlPlane client could not successfully call /api/missions because it did not establish the owner-authenticated cookie session required by the server endpoint.
Local Face ID/device authentication and server owner authentication are distinct trust boundaries; one must not silently substitute for the other.
Do not persist the server owner password merely for convenience; establish a bounded server session and clear the typed password immediately after login.
Do not expose claim, complete, cancel, retry, or dispatch controls from the phone while Qubes worker correctness is still only LAB READY.
Static contract QA protects authority and endpoint semantics but does not replace a native Swift/Xcode build and runtime test.
nextGate: Get DIG Node QA green on the new contract tests, then run a native Swift build/runtime test when an Apple build environment is available. REAL-WORKER readiness remains gated separately on a real Qube-to-Qube qrexec campaign.
